title: What If the Internet Ran Out of Addresses? It Already Did

scenes.text: What if the internet ran out of addresses? It already did, and you probably never noticed.
The original system, called IPv4, has about 4.3 billion addresses, a limit set back in 1981.
On February 3, 2011, the group that hands out addresses announced it had given away the last free blocks.
ARIN, the registry for North America, officially ran out of IPv4 addresses in 2015.
The fix is IPv6, with 128-bit addresses. That's about 340 undecillion, a 340 followed by 36 zeros.
So nothing broke. The internet just moved to a number so big we're very unlikely to run out again.
